newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees telecoms licensing scheme. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: EU agrees telecoms licensing scheme. [CORRECTED 11:30 GMT]

text.p: European Union telecommunications ministers agreed on Friday a regime for licensing telecoms companies once state monopolies are abolished under the EU's liberalisation plan.

The plan, which must be approved by the European Parliament before final adoption, requires governments to use open and objective procedures and establishes a "one-stop shopping" system for companies wanting to operate in more than one EU state.
One of the final sticking points was over when to oblige operators to apply for individual licences and when to allow them to fall under a "general authorisation" scheme requiring no prior approval.

The European Commission wanted to restrict the use of individual licences to cases where governments needed to allocate radio frequencies or numbers, grant access to land or impose public service obligations.
But the ministers decided EU states should be allowed to require individual licences as well for all providers of voice telephone services or public telecommunications networks, EU officials said.

They also agreed that governments should be able to limit the number of operators in a given sector only if needed to ensure the efficient use of radio frequencies or, on a temporary basis, because of a shortage of telephone numbers.
That responded to a request from Spain, which said it needed more time to reorganise its numbering system as required under previous EU legislation.
The text says governments must in principle decide on applications for individual licences within six weeks, although that could be extended up to eight months in cases of competitive bidding.
They must also set up appeal procedures for companies whose bids have been turned down.

EU states would be required to implement the rules by December 31, 1997, (corrects date from December 12, 1997), just in time for the January 1, 1998 EU deadline for liberalising all telecoms sectors in most countries.
